alternates.speaker: King Brihadratha
alternates.setting: The king's plea after listing everything that passes.
alternates.sanskrit: सोऽहमित्येतद्विधेऽस्मिन्संसारे किं कामोपभोगैर्यैरेवाश्रितस्यासकृदिहावर्तनं दृश्यत इत्युद्धर्तुमर्हसीत्यन्धोदपानस्थो भेक इवाहमस्मिन्संसारे भगवंस्त्वं नो गतिस्त्वं नो गतिः ॥
alternates.line: Like a frog in a dark well, I am stuck in this life. Show me the way out.
alternates.translation: In such a world, what use is the enjoyment of desires, when one who feeds on them is seen to return here again and again? Please lift me out. In this world I am like a frog in a dark well. Sir, you are my way, you are my way.
alternates.why: Even success can leave you feeling stuck; asking for help is the first step out.

prasang.title: King Brihadratha's despair
prasang.summary: A king hands his throne to his son and goes to the forest, overwhelmed by how everything decays. When a sage offers him a wish, he says he feels like a frog in a dark well and asks to be shown the way out.
prasang.story_hook: King Brihadratha had everything a king could want, and walked away from all of it.
prasang.lesson: Even success can leave you feeling stuck; asking for help is the first step out.

alternates.speaker: Bhartrihari
alternates.sanskrit: रात्रिः सैव पुनः स एव दिवसो मत्वा मुधा जन्तवो धावन्त्युद्यमिनस्तथैव निभृतप्रारब्धतत्तत्क्रियाः । व्यापारैः पुनरुक्तभूत विषयैरित्थंविधेनामुना संसारेण कदर्थिता वयमहो मोहान्न लज्जामहे ॥
alternates.line: Same night, same day, the same tasks on repeat. We run in circles and call it living.
alternates.translation: Thinking 'it is the same night again, the same day', creatures run about in vain, busy as ever with the tasks they have set going; with work full of the same repeated things, tormented by this round of existence, alas, out of delusion we feel no shame.
alternates.why: Time is passing while you're busy; notice it before it's gone.

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Ashma (quoted by Vyasa)
verse.setting: The sage Ashma answers King Janaka, who asks how to stay steady when people and wealth come and go.
verse.sanskrit: मानसानां पुनर्योनिर्दुःखानां चित्तविभ्रमः / अनिष्टोपनिपातो वा तृतीयं नोपपद्यते
verse.line: Mental pain comes from two places: something you didn't want happened, or your mind is spinning. No third.
verse.translation: Sorrow of the mind has only two sources: a confused, wandering mind, or something unwanted happening to you. There is no third.
verse.why: Days don't come back. Grieve, then steady yourself with the people still in front of you.

prasang.title: Ashma Gita: the sage on bearing loss
prasang.summary: Vyasa tells the grieving Yudhishthira how the sage Ashma consoled King Janaka: pain comes from what we didn't want or what we lost; meetings end; days don't return; ask who you are and steady the mind.
prasang.lesson: Days don't come back. Grieve, then steady yourself with the people still in front of you.

verse.try_today: Notice when the mind begins to spin and ask what it is adding to the day.
verse.scene_line: You stand in the quiet of a full house, and the mind asks what it all was for.

why: Two sources of the mind's pain (Mahabharata, Shanti Parva (Ashma Gita))
Sorts the pain into what happened and what the mind is adding

verse.speaker: Tulsidas
verse.setting: Tulsidas on what is left when every other practice feels out of reach.
verse.sanskrit: नहिं कलि करम न भगति बिबेकू। राम नाम अवलंबन एकू॥ कालनेमि कलि कपट निधानू। नाम सुमति समरथ हनुमानू ॥
verse.line: When no practice, devotion or wisdom seems within reach, the name of Ram is still a support.
verse.translation: In this age there is no ritual action, no devotion and no discernment left to lean on; the name of Ram is the one support. In the age of Kali, the name is the clever Hanuman against Kalanemi, the master of deceit.

verse.for_you: You have the house, the car, the title, and still feel empty. In this age, even devotion can feel out of reach. The name of Ram is the one support that remains, steady and sure.
verse.try_today: Say the name of Ram once, slowly, as you notice the empty feeling today.

why: there is one thing one can still do
when every practice feels beyond one, a support is still left

verse.speaker: Sage Nishakara
verse.setting: The old vulture Sampati, wings burnt and grounded for ages, is told why he should live on.
verse.sanskrit: उत्सहेयमहं कर्तुमद्यैव त्वां सपक्षकम्। इहस्थस्त्वं हि लोकानां हितं कार्यं करिष्यसि॥
verse.line: You are needed exactly where you are, as you are. Your use isn't over.
verse.translation: I could give you back your wings this very day. But by staying here as you are, you will do something for the good of the world.
verse.why: Even when you feel useless, your experience may be exactly what someone needs.

prasang.title: Sampati, the bird who could not fly
prasang.summary: The despairing monkeys meet Sampati, Jatayu's old brother, whose wings burnt long ago. A sage once told him to live on, because one day his knowledge would be needed. Now he tells them Sita is in Lanka, and his wings grow back.
prasang.story_hook: For thousands of years the old bird had sat on a mountain with no wings, waiting for a reason.
prasang.lesson: Even when you feel useless, your experience may be exactly what someone needs.

verse.for_you: You have the house and the car, yet something still feels missing. You have done the hard work of showing up. There is more for you to do here.
verse.try_today: Notice one small thing you are needed for today.
verse.scene_line: You stand in the quiet of the house, and the old vulture waits beside you.

why: a life that feels finished is told it still has a task
'Do not feel small'; someone reminds you who you are.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Arjuna asks which devotee is best; Krishna offers a ladder of practices.
verse.sanskrit: अभ्यासेऽप्यसमर्थोऽसि मत्कर्मपरमो भव । मदर्थमपि कर्माणि कुर्वन् सिद्धिमवाप्स्यसि ॥
verse.line: If even practice is too hard, just do your work for my sake. That alone takes you far.
verse.translation: If you are unable even to practise, be intent on doing work for my sake. Even by doing actions for me, you will reach perfection.
verse.why: If the ideal is too hard, take the next step down, and keep going.

prasang.title: Form or formless: which devotee is best, and the ways to reach him
prasang.summary: Krishna says devotion to a personal form is easier, then offers a ladder: fix your mind; if not, practise; if not, work for me; if not, let go of results. Letting go brings peace at once.
prasang.lesson: If the ideal is too hard, take the next step down, and keep going.

verse.scene_line: You stand in the house you built, and the work of the day continues around you.

why: work done for his sake
If you cannot do that, then this

verse.speaker: Ram
verse.setting: Ram asks Bharat to rule in his place for fourteen years.
verse.sanskrit: जानि तुम्हहि मृदु कहउँ कठोरा। कुसमयँ तात न अनुचित मोरा॥ होहिं कुठायँ सुबंधु सहाए। ओड़िअहिं हाथ असनिहु के धाए ॥
verse.line: In bad times, good siblings are the hands that rise to block the blow.
verse.translation: Knowing you are gentle, I still say something hard; in hard times, brother, it isn't wrong of me. In bad times it is good brothers who help; it is the hands that rise to block a thunderbolt.
verse.why: A good resolution gives each person a role and something to hold on to.

prasang.title: Ram and Bharat settle it
prasang.summary: Ram tells Bharat that keeping their father's word is the duty of both brothers, and that the leader must be like the mouth, taking in only to nourish the whole body. He asks him to rule in his place, knowing it is the harder task. Bharat accepts, asking only for Ram's sandals to keep him going.
prasang.story_hook: Both brothers wanted the other to be king.
prasang.lesson: A good resolution gives each person a role and something to hold on to.

verse.try_today: Let someone else hold the weight of the house for one hour today.
verse.scene_line: You stand in the empty house while the hands of the ones you love rise to shield you from the thunderbolt.

why: taking the hard share for one's family when times are bad

story.title: Shiva's grief turns to Ram's name
story.story_hook: When Sati was gone, the great god of the mountains did not rage or hide; he walked, and he kept saying a name.
story.summary: After Sati is gone, Shiva wanders, teaching and singing of Ram, repeating his name. Though beyond desire, he still grieves the loss of his devotee. Seeing his steady love, Ram appears, grateful and kind, praises Shiva's vow and asks him to marry Parvati.
story.lesson: Grief and devotion can walk together; steady love in loss is seen.
story.hook_title: When Sati was gone, Shiva walked and kept saying one name
story.teaser: When Sati was gone, Shiva walked and kept saying one name
story.for_you: The years of work and the house and the car have left you feeling small and empty, wondering what it was all for. You do not have to reason this away. Let the grief sit with you and be carried into the sound of the name and the company of those who remember it.

why: Grief is not reasoned away; it is carried into remembrance and good company until it loosens.

verse.speaker: Nidagha
verse.sanskrit: पदं करोत्यलङ्घ्येऽपि तृप्ता विफलमीहते । चिरं तिष्ठति नैकत्र तृष्णा चपलमर्कटी ॥
verse.line: Craving is a restless monkey: never in one place, never satisfied, reaching even where it cannot go.
verse.translation: It sets foot even where no one can go; even when satisfied it strives in vain; it never stays long in one place: craving is a restless monkey.
verse.why: Naming how restless your mind is, is where peace begins.

prasang.title: Nidagha's lament
prasang.summary: Young Nidagha returns from pilgrimage disillusioned and pours out his heart to his teacher Ribhu: life is fleeting, the mind runs like a stray dog, craving gnaws every good quality, and mastering the mind is harder than drinking the ocean.
prasang.lesson: Naming how restless your mind is, is where peace begins.

verse.for_you: You have built a good house and a good name. Still, the wanting runs everywhere, chewing through what is already there.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment when you are satisfied and the mind still reaches for more.
verse.scene_line: You sit in the house you built, and the craving reaches even where no one can go.

why: wanting that keeps going even after it has been fed
My mind runs everywhere for nothing, and every good quality I take up, craving chews through. What do I do?

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: आशा नाम नदी मनोरथजला तृष्णातरङ्गाकुला रागग्राहवती वितर्कविहगा धैर्यद्रुमध्वंसिनी । मोहावर्तसुदुस्तरातिगहना प्रोत्तुङ्गचिन्तातटी तस्याः पारगता विशुद्धमनसो नन्दन्ति योगीश्वराः ॥
verse.line: Hope is a river: its water is wishes, its waves are craving, and its high banks are worry.
verse.translation: There is a river called Hope. Its water is wishes, its waves are craving; passions are its crocodiles, doubts its birds; it uproots the trees of courage; its whirlpools of delusion are hard to cross and deep, and its banks of worry tower high. Only great yogis, pure in mind, who reach the far shore, rejoice.
verse.why: We think we are chasing things; really, the chase is using up our lives.

prasang.title: Vairagyashatakam: Censure of craving
prasang.summary: The poet confesses everything he did for money and approval: digging for treasure, flattering kings, forcing laughter. He ends with the famous lines that pleasures consumed us and craving never aged, and hope pictured as a river.
prasang.lesson: We think we are chasing things; really, the chase is using up our lives.

verse.for_you: You have the house, the car, the title after ten years of fourteen-hour days, yet the finish line feels empty. The river of hope you swam in was made of wishes and craving, and the high banks of worry finally wore you down. Rest in the quiet truth that you have reached the shore.
verse.try_today: Notice one wish rising like a wave, and let it pass without crossing the bank.
verse.scene_line: Bhartrihari watches you stand on the high banks of worry, with the house and car behind you on the shore.

why: The river called Hope (Bhartrihari, Vairagya Shataka 10)
Craving as the waves

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verse.sanskrit: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन । मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥
verse.line: Your work is yours to do; the results are not yours to hold. Don't let that make you stop.
verse.translation: Your right is to the work alone, never to its fruits. Do not let the fruit be your motive, and do not cling to doing nothing.

words.en: cause of the fruit of action

verse.why: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.
verse.misuse: This is not 'don't care about results' or 'don't plan'. Care, plan and aim well; just don't let the outcome own you.

matched.label: I'm burned out and running on empty

prasang.title: The yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

verse.for_you: You have spent a decade giving every hour to a life that looks full on paper. The title and the car are yours, but the emptiness is also yours. Your work was yours to do, and the feeling of emptiness is not yours to hold.
verse.try_today: Let the next task be the only reason you do it.
verse.scene_line: You stand in a quiet house after a long day of work that was yours alone.

why: the fruit is taken away as the reason for acting
Work done with huge strain for ego or pleasure is rajasic.

verse.speaker: Pingala (quoted by Bhishma)
verse.setting: Pingala, left waiting all night by a lover who never came, finally lets go and finds peace.
verse.sanskrit: सुखं निराशः स्वपिति नैराश्यं परमं सुखम् / आशामनाशां कृत्वा हि सुखं स्वपिति पिङ्गला
verse.line: Pingala let go of her expectation and slept peacefully. Letting go of expectation is the greatest ease.
verse.translation: The one free of expectation sleeps in peace; freedom from expectation is the highest happiness. Turning hope into no-hope, Pingala sleeps peacefully.
verse.why: Letting go of an expectation can bring the sleep that waiting never will.
verse.misuse: This is about clinging to an outcome, not about giving up hope in life.

prasang.title: Pingala's song: the night she stopped waiting
prasang.summary: Pingala waited all night for a lover who never came. At last she saw that her peace depended on someone else's arrival, let the expectation go, and slept peacefully.
prasang.story_hook: Pingala sat awake listening for footsteps that never came, until she stopped listening.
prasang.lesson: Letting go of an expectation can bring the sleep that waiting never will.

verse.try_today: Notice one moment today where you are waiting for the next achievement to feel whole.

why: Dropping the expectation is the ease.
The waiting itself is shown as the pain, and its end as rest

verse.speaker: Seer
verse.setting: How a householder becomes a 'world' for others.
verse.sanskrit: यन्मनुष्यान्वासयते यदेभ्योऽशनं ददाति तेन मनुष्याणामथ यत्पशुभ्यस्तृणोदकं विन्दति तेन पशूनां यदस्य गृहेषु श्वापदा वयाꣳस्या पिपीलिकाभ्य उपजीवन्ति तेन तेषां लोको
verse.line: Feed people, find water for animals; when even ants live off your home, you become a world for them.
verse.translation: By housing people and giving them food, he becomes a world for people. By finding grass and water for animals, he becomes a world for animals. When beasts, birds and even ants live off his house, he becomes a world for them.
verse.for_you: The house, the car, the title, and the fourteen-hour days have not filled you. They have left you empty. You can become a world for others, and in doing so, you become a world for yourself.
verse.try_today: Offer one small thing to another living thing today.
verse.scene_line: You stand in a house that feeds people and animals, yet you feel like a ghost in your own world.

why: Become a world for others.
feeding and housing others is what makes a home a world

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: परिभ्रमसि किं मुधा क्वचन चित्त विश्राम्यतां स्वयं भवति यद्यथा भवति तत्तथा नान्यथा । अतीतमननुस्मरन्नपि च भाव्यसंकल्पयन् नतर्कितसमागमाननुभवामि भोगानहम् ॥
verse.line: Why wander, mind? Rest. Not replaying the past, not scripting the future, I take what comes.
verse.translation: Why do you wander about in vain, mind? Rest somewhere. Whatever is to happen happens just as it will, and not otherwise. Not recalling the past, not planning the future, I enjoy the pleasures that come to me unlooked-for.
verse.why: Stop seeking approval and rehearsing outcomes; the calm you want is already inside.
verse.misuse: Not an argument against planning; it is for the worry loop once you have done your part.

prasang.title: Vairagyashatakam: Advice to the mind
prasang.summary: The poet talks to his own mind: why exhaust yourself pleasing others, why replay the past and script the future, why roam everywhere but within. 'So what?' asks what all our gains amount to.
prasang.lesson: Stop seeking approval and rehearsing outcomes; the calm you want is already inside.

verse.for_you: You have the house, the car, and the title, yet you feel empty. The mind keeps replaying the past and scripting the future instead of resting in what is here now. You take what comes without rehearsing it.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment today where your mind wanders to the past or future, and gently return to what is here.
verse.scene_line: You sit in the quiet of your own life, holding the title you earned, and wonder what it was all for.

why: Enjoying what arrives unplanned
Vishramyatam

story.title: Manki's song: desire, I know your root
story.story_hook: Manki put every coin he had into two young oxen, and lost both in a single afternoon.
story.summary: Manki spends all he has on a pair of oxen; both are killed in an accident. In his despair he sees through desire: it is born of his own imagining, and he resolves to forgive insults and stop feeding it. Bhishma adds Janaka's verse on owning nothing.
story.lesson: Desire grows from what we imagine. Stop feeding it, and it fades.
story.teaser: Manki put every coin he had into two young oxen, and lost both in a single afternoon.

why: Craving is born of one's own imagining; stop feeding it and it dies at the root.

queries.hook: The wish to understand what these texts teach, and to find in them something steady to lean on.
queries.diagnose: When life is lived only for what passes, the heart feels empty; meaning is missing when we forget what does not pass.
queries.steady: What passes cannot fill the heart; turning toward what lasts gives each day a quiet purpose.

plan_v3.first_line: You have built the house, the car, and the title, and still this emptiness dries you up inside like a grief no kingdom could touch.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.setting: From the opening section, 'Censure of Craving': the poet addresses his own craving.
verse.sanskrit: उत्खातं निधिशङ्कया क्षितितलं ध्माता गिरेर्धातवो निस्तीर्णः सरितां पतिर्नृपतयो यत्नेन संतोषिताः । मन्त्राराधनतत्परेण मनसा नीताः श्मशाने निशाः प्राप्तः काणवराटकोऽपि न मया तृष्णे सकामा भव ॥
verse.line: I dug, sailed, flattered kings, chased every scheme, and gained not a broken coin. Enough, craving.
verse.translation: I dug up the earth hoping for treasure, smelted the ores of mountains, crossed the ocean, lord of rivers, worked hard to please kings, spent nights in cremation grounds with my mind fixed on mantras, and I did not get even a broken cowrie. Craving, be satisfied now!
verse.why: We think we are chasing things; really, the chase is using up our lives.

prasang.title: Vairagyashatakam: Censure of craving
prasang.summary: The poet confesses everything he did for money and approval: digging for treasure, flattering kings, forcing laughter. He ends with the famous lines that pleasures consumed us and craving never aged, and hope pictured as a river.
prasang.lesson: We think we are chasing things; really, the chase is using up our lives.

verse.for_you: You built the house and earned the title, and still the rooms feel hollow. You gave your years to schemes that promised everything. Enough. Let the wanting rest for today.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment today when you stop chasing and simply stay with what is already here.
verse.scene_line: You stand in the quiet house you built, and you ask what it was all for.

why: Years of chasing told in first person
The tired 'enough' at the end

verse.speaker: Ashtavakra
verse.setting: Ashtavakra's 'special instruction' to Janaka on why striving and study do not bring peace.
verse.sanskrit: आयासात्सकलो दुःखी नैनं जानाति कश्चन । अनेनैवोपदेशेन धन्यः प्राप्नोति निर्वृतिम् ॥
verse.line: Everyone suffers from constant straining, and no one notices. Seeing this alone brings peace.
verse.translation: Everyone is miserable from straining after things, and no one realises it. By this single teaching the fortunate one finds peace.
verse.why: Peace isn't another achievement; strain less, and stop expecting escape to fix you.
verse.misuse: Not against effort; against the anxious straining that rides on it.

prasang.title: Why striving and study do not bring peace
prasang.summary: Ashtavakra warns that reading scriptures, working or meditating will not bring peace on their own; everyone suffers from straining, and running away from the world doesn't end pain. Even pride in being free is just more suffering.
prasang.lesson: Peace isn't another achievement; strain less, and stop expecting escape to fix you.

verse.try_today: Notice one moment today when you strain, and let it be without fixing it.
verse.scene_line: Ashtavakra speaks to Janaka, and the room holds no one else but you.

why: Where craving is, the round is (Ashtavakra Gita 10.3)
names the straining itself as the cause of the misery

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the inner happiness of one who sees clearly.
verse.sanskrit: बाह्यस्पर्शेष्वसक्तात्मा विन्दत्यात्मनि यत्सुखम् । स ब्रह्मयोगयुक्तात्मा सुखमक्षयमश्नुते ॥
verse.line: Unhooked from outside pleasures, you find a joy within that doesn't run out.
verse.translation: One whose self is unattached to outer contacts finds the happiness that is in the self. Joined to Brahman by yoga, he enjoys undying happiness.
verse.why: Pleasures that start and end can't hold your happiness; find the joy within.

prasang.title: The yoga of knowledge
prasang.summary: Krishna describes the wise: equal-eyed towards all beings, not elated or crushed, finding joy within, seeing that sense pleasures end in sorrow, and able to withstand desire and anger.
prasang.lesson: Pleasures that start and end can't hold your happiness; find the joy within.

verse.for_you: After ten years of long days, the house and the title feel hollow. You have built a life that looks complete but leaves you empty inside. There is a quiet joy waiting for you that does not run out.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment today where you are not seeking anything from the outside.

why: the search turns inward
when outer things stop satisfying, the verse points to a happiness that was never outside

verse.speaker: Prajapati's teaching (narrator)
verse.setting: On the self in the heart that we visit nightly in deep sleep without knowing it.
verse.sanskrit: अनृतापिधानास्तद्यथापि हिरण्यनिधिं निहितमक्षेत्रज्ञा उपर्युपरि सञ्चरन्तो न विन्देयुरेवमेवेमाः सर्वाः प्रजा अहरहर्गच्छन्त्य एतं ब्रह्मलोकं न विन्दन्त्यनृतेन हि प्रत्यूढाः ॥
verse.line: Like people walking daily over buried gold, we pass our own treasure every day and never find it.
verse.translation: As people who do not know the spot walk again and again over a hidden treasure of gold buried in the ground and do not find it, so all these creatures go day after day into that world of Brahman and do not find it, for they are carried away by untruth.

matched.label: Nothing is wrong but nothing feels meaningful

why: the sense that nothing is here is answered: the treasure is under your own feet
no one is poorer in this than anyone else; everyone carries the same gold

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on simple, wholehearted devotion.
verse.sanskrit: यत्करोषि यदश्नासि यज्जुहोषि ददासि यत् । यत्तपस्यसि कौन्तेय तत्कुरुष्व मदर्पणम् ॥
verse.line: Whatever you do, eat, give or endure, do it as an offering.
verse.translation: Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer, whatever you give, whatever austerity you practise, Kaunteya, do it as an offering to me.
verse.why: Small offerings given with love matter; no one is beyond turning around.

prasang.title: The glory of selfless devotion
prasang.summary: A leaf, flower, fruit or water offered with love is accepted. Offer everything you do; the divine hates no one, and even a wrongdoer who turns wholeheartedly is counted good.
prasang.lesson: Small offerings given with love matter; no one is beyond turning around.

verse.try_today: Notice one small action today, like drinking water or starting the car, and offer it as you would a flower.
verse.scene_line: You stand in the quiet of your success, and Krishna offers you the next task as a flower.

why: work as offering

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: A powerful king offers a fortune for the sage's cow, the source of his whole way of life.
verse.sanskrit: नाहं शतसहस्रेण नापि कोटिशतैर्गवाम्॥ राजन् दास्यामि शबलां राशिभी रजतस्य वा। न परित्यागमयं मत्सकाशादरिंदम ॥
verse.line: Not for any price. Some things are not for sale, however powerful the buyer.
verse.translation: Not for a hundred thousand cows, not for a billion, not for heaps of silver, O king, will I give up Shabala. She stays with me.
verse.why: Envy and force cannot take what someone will not give; real power is built inside.

prasang.title: The king who wanted the cow
prasang.summary: King Vishvamitra is feasted by the sage Vasishtha and covets the wish-granting cow that made it possible. Vasishtha refuses every offer; the king takes her by force and is routed, then fails again with divine weapons. Humbled, he resolves to transform himself through inner discipline instead of force.
prasang.story_hook: A king who had everything saw one thing he could not buy, and it undid him.
prasang.lesson: Envy and force cannot take what someone will not give; real power is built inside.

verse.for_you: You have the house and the title, but the thing that sustains your life is not for sale. It stays with you, and that is enough for today.
verse.try_today: Notice what sustains you today that no price could buy.
verse.scene_line: You stand before a king offering a fortune, yet the thing that sustains your rites stays with you.

why: what sustains his life is not for sale
